subject: Embeddings p99 regressions after catalog refresh — urgent customer report
messages:
From: Maddy Chen <maddy@searchoria.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, support@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@searchoria.com, Evan Liu <evan@searchoria.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: sudden embeddings latency increase since catalog update

Hi Rachel / Redwood team,

We started seeing a large jump in embedding latencies right after the model catalog refresh this morning (around 08:45 PST). Our p95 for the embeddings endpoint went from ~180ms to ~1.2s and p99s are regularly above 2s. Also seeing transient 502/504s when traffic is above ~120 qps. This is affecting our similarity ranking and search recency—several jobs failed in production.

Quick details:
- API: POST /v1/embeddings (batch size ~8)
- Example request id: req_8f3a2b6d
- We haven't changed client-side code; nothing on our side changed this morning.
- This coincided with your public model catalog update at 08:40 PST (we got the webhook).

I've attached a small trace log and a p99 chart snapshot. Can you confirm whether any default model variant or routing changed for the hosted embeddings endpoint? We need an interim mitigation (rollback or pin to previous model) and an ETA for a fix—this is blocking search for a subset of users.

Thanks,
Maddy Chen
Head of Engineering, Searchoria
Attachments: searchoria_traces_20260214.txt, p99_sla_graph_20260214.png

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>

- Vivek/Marcus: immediate mitigation options (pin to prev model, route their traffic to dedicated pool, or rollback catalog change globally).
- Hannah/Sean: customer comms and SLA protections (we may need to offer credits).

I'll stand by for updates — please flag if you need exec escalation.

—Rachel

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, eng-incident@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 14 Feb 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: sudden embeddings latency increase since catalog update — Searchoria (urgent)

Thanks for flagging — quick summary of what I'm seeing from infra: the catalog refresh at 08:40 introduced a new default embedding variant for the "embed-large" family: embed-large-quant-v2. That variant routes to a different kernel path which enables a CPU fallback when GPU quant kernels are overloaded. Two problems:
1) Dynamic kernel selection thresholds were set conservatively; under steady ~100-150 qps the new path forces small-batch CPU offload which increases tail latency (p99).
2) The routing policy for hosted tenants didn't pin test customers; some traffic was transparently shifted.

Immediate mitigations we can do now (ranked):
- 1) Pin Searchoria's routing to the previous model variant (embed-large-quant-v1) for the next 12h. Quick config change, near-zero risk.
- 2) Disable the new kernel selection globally until we've tuned thresholds. Requires infra approval and short maintenance window.
- 3) Route Searchoria to an isolated dedicated pool (capacity permitting) — slower to stand up but isolates risk.

I've prepared the rollback command to revert the catalog default for embeddings; ready to run on your go. I can also push a routing override for the tenant now which will take effect within 60s.

Logs attached: svc_logs_20260214.zip (redwood agent traces showing kernel selection jitter).

Propose: apply tenant pin now, prepare global rollback if customer impact persists.

—Vivek
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Immediate comms plan for Searchoria: short acknowledgement now, motion to set expectation (we're rolling back/pinning and will follow up with a fix + postmortem). Offer: provisional 10% service credit for the impacted 24h window while we investigate — keep it limited until we confirm scope.

I'll prepare a short note to Maddy with an ETA (30–60m for mitigation). Rachel, want me to send the outbound?

—Hannah
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: eng-incident@redwood.ai, monitoring@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 14 Feb 2026 15:00:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: sudden embeddings latency increase since catalog update — Searchoria (mitigation update)

Update — actions taken:
- 14:12 PST: applied tenant routing override to pin Searchoria to embed-large-quant-v1. Effects visible within ~60s.
- 14:35 PST: observed p95 drop back to ~210ms; p99 reduced and stabilized around 350–400ms.
- 14:50 PST: rolled back global default for embed-large family as a precaution.

Remaining: traces show occasional KV cache key mismatch for some requests leading to a small number of 504s; these are much lower frequency than earlier. We are running a TTL revalidation job and monitoring.

Next steps: continue monitoring for 24h, run a stress test tomorrow using the previous traffic mix, tune kernel selection thresholds before re-enabling the new variant. I'll own the postmortem and will link the draft when done.

—Marcus Lin
Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Maddy Chen <maddy@searchoria.com>, Evan Liu <evan@searchoria.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 17:45:00 -0800
Subject: Searchoria — post-incident update and next steps

Hi Maddy / Evan,

Thank you again for your patience while we investigated the embeddings latency spike you reported on Saturday. Summary of what happened and what we did:

What happened:
- On Feb 14 at ~08:40 PST a model catalog refresh promoted a new embedding variant (embed-large-quant-v2) with updated kernel selection heuristics.
- Under Searchoria's production traffic profile that change caused frequent CPU fallback for small batches, increasing tail latency and causing some 5xxs at higher concurrency.

What we did:
- We applied a tenant routing override to pin you to the previous variant (embed-large-quant-v1) at 14:12 PST on Feb 14.
- We rolled back the global catalog default and ran a targeted fix for the kernel selection thresholds.
- Marcus is owning a postmortem and we’ve run additional stress tests; we will not re-enable the new variant for hosted customers until thresholds are tuned and we validate at scale.

Compensation and follow-up:
- We are offering a provisional 10% credit for the impacted 24-hour window (subject to final scope confirmation). Hannah from CS will coordinate paperwork.
- I’ll schedule a 30-minute technical review with Marcus and Vivek to walk through the postmortem and confirm the re-enablement plan — proposed time: Wed Feb 18 10:00 PST.

Attachments: p99_sla_graph_20260214.png, postmortem_draft_linked_in_related_links

We sincerely apologize for the disruption. Please let us know if you want an immediate deeper dive or different remediation.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
